goal: Make isValidScope in src/delivery/asgi-core-profile.mjs reject structurally invalid ASGI HTTP scopes at the profile boundary, before StandardRouter or receive() ever see them. Before this package, isValidScope only checked that scope.method and scope.path were strings, so an empty method (''), an empty path (''), or a path without a leading slash (e.g. 'customers') passed the profile check and reached StandardRouter, which would answer with an ordinary 404/405 router response instead of the frozen 400 PROFILE_SCOPE_INVALID profile-error response every other malformed-scope shape already gets. This package closes that gap so all structurally invalid HTTP scopes are rejected uniformly at the profile boundary.
nonGoals: no new dependency, listener, HTTP/net/fs capability, environment read, clock or randomness use
no change to valid-scope routing behavior, response shapes, header encoding, or query_string handling
no path normalization, decoding, or semantic validation beyond the non-empty/leading-slash structural check

scopeResolution.note: Minimal production fix: isValidScope now additionally requires scope.method.length > 0, scope.path.length > 0, and scope.path.startsWith('/'). No router, receive, or response-encoding logic touched.

red.note: Added three scope shapes to the existing malformed-scope test (empty method, empty path, path without leading slash 'customers') plus a new dedicated callFromReceive test proving a leading-slash-missing path short-circuits to the 400 profile response without ever calling receive(). Against the pre-fix source, the malformed-scope test failed with 404 !== 400 (StandardRouter answered instead of the profile boundary), and the new callFromReceive test failed the same way, proving the profile boundary was leaking these shapes to the router.

green.results: All 36 tests pass, including the new empty-method, empty-path, missing-leading-slash, and callFromReceive-does-not-call-receive assertions. npm run check exits GREEN with no new failures. Existing valid /customers behavior and query_string-ignored behavior are unchanged.

acceptance.emptyMethodRejected: scope.method === '' returns the frozen 400 PROFILE_SCOPE_INVALID profile response instead of reaching StandardRouter
acceptance.emptyPathRejected: scope.path === '' returns the frozen 400 PROFILE_SCOPE_INVALID profile response instead of reaching StandardRouter
acceptance.pathWithoutLeadingSlashRejected: scope.path values like 'customers' (no leading slash) return the frozen 400 PROFILE_SCOPE_INVALID profile response instead of reaching StandardRouter
acceptance.callFromReceiveDoesNotCallReceiveOnInval: callFromReceive short-circuits to the 400 profile response for an invalid path before ever invoking receive()
acceptance.validScopeUnchanged: existing valid-scope routing, response encoding, and query_string-ignored behavior are byte-identical to before this package

rollback.trigger: the added structural checks are found to reject a scope shape that must be valid, or any existing test regresses
rollback.action: revert the three added conditions in isValidScope, the added test assertions/test, this planning file and the CHANGELOG entry as one shard
rollback.blastRadius: one function (isValidScope) inside src/delivery/asgi-core-profile.mjs; no other function or file touched
rollback.runtimeDataImpact: none; no runtime, DB, or I/O surface involved

capabilityDelta: ASGI_PROFILE_SCOPE_STRUCTURAL_CONFORMANCE: the profile boundary now rejects empty method, empty path, and path-without-leading-slash HTTP scopes uniformly as 400 PROFILE_SCOPE_INVALID, before router or receive ever run, instead of letting some of these shapes leak through to StandardRouter as an ordinary 404/405.
